title: The scheme of finite open parts containing a section
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] in the universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be an $S$-morphism of schemes which is separated (its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-proper-morphism]), flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and let $\sigma:Y\to X$ satisfy $f\sigma=\mathrm{id}_Y$. On $S$-schemes $T$, define $\mathcal F(T)$ to consist of pairs $(a,Z)$ with $a:T\to Y$ and $Z\subseteq X\times_{f,Y,a}T$ an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion, def-pc-fibre-product], finite over $T$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], through which $(\sigma a,\mathrm{id}_T)$ factors. Pullback of pairs along $T'\to T$ defines the functor. There is an $S$-scheme $M$ representing $\mathcal F$: natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_S(T,M)\simeq\mathcal F(T)$ identify composition into a morphism $g:M\to Y$ with forgetting $Z$. The morphism $g$ is separated and etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Its universal subscheme $Z_{\mathrm{univ}}\subseteq X\times_YM$ is open and closed, finite over $M$, and contains the base change of $\sigma$. For every $y\in Y$ such that $f$ is quasi-finite at $\sigma(y)$ [pqf-def-quasifinite], there is $m\in M$ with $g(m)=y$ and with induced residue-field map $\kappa(y)\to\kappa(m)$ an isomorphism [def-weil-residue-field]. The schemes can be taken in the chosen universe.

source.place: Tags 04RI (lemma-finite-separated-flat-locally-finite-presentation), 04RR (lemma-finite-plus-section), and 04RW (lemma-quasi-splitting), final paragraph, the section-marked finite-part construction applied to a general morphism with section. Universal open is closed by lemma-finite-separated.

proof.text: A finitely presented algebra is generated by its finitely many polynomial variables; thus $f$ is locally of finite type. Apply [lem-sfb-unmarked-finite-open-parts-space] to obtain the unmarked algebraic space $p:E\to Y$ and its chartwise etaleness. We will first prove $p$ separated, then obtain a scheme before evaluating a universal pair on it.

For any scheme test $a:T\to Y$ and finite open $Z\subseteq X_T$, the projection $X_T\to T$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-lqf-base-change](1). The finite map $Z\to T$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres](1). Applying [lemma-nagata-proper-to-separated-target] to $Z\to X_T\to T$ shows that the inclusion has closed image. Since $Z$ already has its open subscheme structure, it is an open and closed subscheme. This holds for every test and will apply to the universal pair once its base is a scheme.

source.place: Tag 04PH (lemma-finite-separated); scheme proof via morphisms.tex Tag 01W6(2).

proof.text: Test the diagonal of $p$ by two pairs $(a,Z_1),(a,Z_2)$ over a scheme $T$. In $X_T$ put $D_1=Z_1\setminus Z_2$ and $D_2=Z_2\setminus Z_1$. Step 2 makes each $D_i$ open and closed in $Z_i$. Its image $B_i\subseteq T$ is closed since $Z_i\to T$ is finite. It is also open: the projections $Z_i\to T$ are flat by base change and restriction to an open (the local rings are unchanged), and locally of finite presentation by base change and open restriction. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open]. Put $B=B_1\cup B_2$ and $V=T\setminus B$. Under any $h:T'\to T$, the two pulled-back opens agree exactly when both pulled-back differences are empty; [lem-weil-pbc-base-change-image] identifies their images with $h^{-1}(B_i)$. Thus equality holds exactly when $h$ factors through $V$. Since $B$ is open and closed, $V\hookrightarrow T$ is a closed immersion. These are precisely all scheme tests of the diagonal, so $p$ is separated. The hypotheses of [lem-a1-separated-etale-space-scheme] now hold; hence $E$ is a scheme, and $p$ is etale.

source.place: Tag 04RI, equality-locus argument and final schemehood paragraph. The source writes T-prime where the test base is T; the construction here uses T consistently.

proof.text: The identity of the scheme $E$ corresponds to $(p,C)$ with $C\subseteq X\times_YE$ finite and open. Let $s_E:E\to X\times_YE$ be the base-changed section and set $M=s_E^{-1}(C)$ with its induced open subscheme structure. Step 2 makes $C$, hence $M$, closed as well. For $h:T\to E$, the section of $X_T$ factors through $h^*C$ exactly when $h$ factors through $M$; therefore $M$ represents precisely the requested marked pairs, naturally under pullback. Its map $g$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](1),(2). Its diagonal is the pullback of the closed diagonal of $p$ to $M\times_YM$, so $g$ is separated. The universal $Z_{\mathrm{univ}}=C\times_EM$ is finite, open and closed and contains the section, by its construction and base change.

source.place: Tag 04RR (lemma-finite-plus-section), hint expanded by taking the inverse image of the universal open; universal pair from equation-finite.

proof.text: Fix $y$ and put $x=\sigma(y)$ and $k=\kappa(y)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-at-point-isolated] $x$ is isolated in $X_y$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-finite-at-point-elementary] to $f,x$: obtain $(U,u)\to(Y,y)$ with $\kappa(u)=k$ and a finite open $A\subseteq X_U$ containing the unique fibre point $v$ over $u$ mapping to $x$. Pull back along the canonical $\operatorname{Spec}k\to U$. This gives a finite open $Z\subseteq X_y$ containing the fibre point over $x$. The fibre projection has a unique point over $x$, so this is exactly the image of the section $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X_y$; that section factors through $Z$ by the defining factorization property of an open subscheme. The represented pair $(y,Z)$ gives $q:\operatorname{Spec}k\to M$ with $gq=y$. Let $m=q(*)$ and let $a:k\to\kappa(m)$ and $b:\kappa(m)\to k$ be the residue maps. The field-point description and residue-map naturality give $ba=1_k$. A field homomorphism $b$ is injective, so $b(ab(t))=b(t)$ implies $ab(t)=t$ for every $t\in\kappa(m)$. Hence $a$ is an isomorphism, proving the required residue-field clause.

source.place: Tag 04RW (lemma-quasi-splitting), fibre finite-part paragraph; the finite fibre piece is supplied by more-morphisms.tex Tag 02LK. Residue-field interpretation: schemes.tex Tag 01J9.

proof.text: Use the universe-sized atlas in [lem-sfb-unmarked-finite-open-parts-space]. Schemehood glues charts of this atlas, and $M$ and $Z_{\mathrm{univ}}$ are open subschemes of schemes obtained by fibre products from the given ones. The set of charts, their open subsets, their rings and their gluing relations belong to the fixed Grothendieck universe, which is closed under these set constructions. Thus the representing schemes can be taken in the chosen universe.
